title: Beyond the 956: Marty Erlichman, Barbra Streisand's manager of 60 years, dies at 97

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Marty Erlichman, the entertainment manager who discovered Barbra Streisand and guided her career for more than 60 years, has died at 97.

Erlichman died Saturday, October 31, 2026, in Los Angeles of age-related causes, Variety and The Hollywood Reporter reported November 1. He was 97.

Erlichman was born Martin Lee Erlichman on September 13, 1929, in Brooklyn, New York, and graduated from Drake University. His life changed in 1961, when he saw a young Streisand sing in a Manhattan nightclub and bought out her existing management contract. The two worked together for more than six decades — Streisand's only manager — on what she has described as a handshake, with no contract.

He negotiated her recording, theater, film, television, licensing and concert agreements as she rose from nightclub singer to Broadway star, Grammy winner and Oscar winner. He conceived and executive produced her landmark concerts, including the 2000 Millennium Concert and her 2006–2007 world tour, and executive produced her 1994 HBO special Barbra: The Concert, which won him an Emmy Award and a Peabody Award. His film credits as a producer included Streisand's 1974 comedy For Pete's Sake, the 1978 thriller Coma and the 1983 thriller Breathless.

Streisand said in a statement: "Although Marty lived a long and full life, nothing can prepare you for the reality of losing someone so dear. I truly thought he would live forever. He can never be replaced, and I will be forever grateful for his friendship, loyalty, and unwavering support." His family said in a statement carried by The Hollywood Reporter: "To the world, he was a giant of Hollywood; to us, he was a deeply devoted and loving father, husband, grandfather and rock."

Erlichman is survived by his wife, Miko Mayama Erlichman, and their son, J.J.

Rest in Peace, Marty Erlichman.

Sources: Variety; The Hollywood Reporter.
